newsitem.title: INDIA: More than 300 feared dead in Indian floods.
newsitem.headline: More than 300 feared dead in Indian floods.

text.p: At least 326 people were feared dead in floods that ravaged vast areas of agricultural land in India's southern state of Andhra Pradesh, officials said on Wednesday.
Seven days of floods caused by heavy rains destroyed thousands of homes and washed away agricultural land, forcing the evacuation of nearly 100,000 people now sheltering in 120 relief camps.

Officials said more than a million hectares (2.5 million acres) of groundnut, 200,000 hectares (500,000 acres) of cotton, 200,000 hectares of paddy, about 75,000 hectares (187,500 acres) of chillis and 25,000 hectares (62,500 acres) of horticultural crops have been damaged.
Andhra Pradesh state Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu put preliminary estimates of crop losses at four billion rupees ($112 million).
Army boats helped in the civilian rescue operation while air force helicopters dropped food to stranded villagers in devastated areas.
Flooding also affected neighbouring Tamil Nadu state.
Officials said on Tuesday more than 38,000 people, mostly farmers and fishermen, had been rescued by troops from low-lying coastal areas in both states facing the Bay of Bengal.
